text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:

- The Israeli parliament will take on the issue of unclaimed funds that might have been left in Swiss banks after World War Two as a reaction to a comment by a Swiss member of government who rejected the idea of creating a 250 million Swiss franc fund for Holocaust victims before a thorough investigation of any dormant accounts on Swiss banks.
- Swiss banks are concerned after boycott threats by Jewish organisations. The shares of leading Swiss finance institutes fell on Monday.

- The smallest cultural group in Switzerland, the Raetian people, received for the first time in its history a newspaper written in Rhaeto-Romanic. It is called 'La Quotidiana' and will be published daily.
- Swiss construction permit requests dropped by two percent in 1996 compared to the previous year.
- The Cantonal Bank of Basle has broken a taboo by opening a representational office in Zurich.
